LOGSCOPE / CLIENT EVALUATION 1.1.0

From log files
to a reviewable decision.

Analyze a batch, inspect the evidence and record what happens next. This guide covers the delivered workspace and its operating limits.

1. Choose the right input

Select HDFS, BGL or OpenStack and click Load sample. OpenStack offers an annotated failure run and the original normal-only sample. The dashboard uses these bundled inputs.

The included CLI and Flask API also support custom log/CSV inputs. Optional labels can be supplied with LineId,Label, using 0 for normal and 1 for anomalous. HDFS also supports BlockId,Label. Open Configure to attach labels and choose analysis settings.

2. Run and evaluate

Click Run analysis. The first on-device run downloads the Python runtime and scientific packages and may take a minute. Settings stay locked until the run finishes or you cancel. Cancelling on-device analysis stops its worker; cancelling navigation does not cancel a server job.

Sample results shown before a run are measured bundled results, clearly marked as a sample. Fresh results reflect your current input and configuration. Open Evaluation to see held-out precision, recall, F1 and confusion counts. The training interval precedes the test interval. Scores are not probabilities.

HDFS uses official block labels mapped to time windows. OpenStack defaults to an annotated failure run, with labels derived from association with four annotated VMs. The original OpenStack 2k sample contains normal labels only: recall and F1 are unavailable by design. Missing labels are not silently converted to normal.

3. Investigate and document

Open Incident worklist, review a flagged window, then record its owner, investigation notes and status. Click Save and check the save feedback. A flagged window is a candidate for investigation, not a confirmed incident. Notes and owners are free text; owner assignment does not send notifications.

The worklist filters open, acknowledged and resolved candidates. Use Client report for a printable HTML report, then your browser's Print → Save as PDF. Use Incident CSV for all candidates and notes, and Results JSON for complete analytical output. Reports exclude raw log messages; JSON and other exports can contain log evidence.

Where your work is stored

On-device analysis: computation runs in your browser; run history uses IndexedDB and triage uses local browser storage. Work is specific to this browser and origin. Browser cleanup, private browsing or storage limits can remove it. Export anything you need to retain.

Server analysis: when running the supplied Flask application, analysis, models and triage are stored in its SQLite database. Use Server access if your administrator configured an API token. Tokens are held in this tab's session storage. The hosted website is the on-device version; it does not provide a shared Flask server.

When something goes wrong

  • No evaluation: verify label coverage and both label classes. Re-run after attaching labels. Normal-only input cannot measure anomaly recall.
  • Rejected rows: check parser, timestamps and CSV columns in the data quality view. Keep the original file.
  • Runtime cannot load: check network access to runtime package CDNs and retry. The supplied Python/Flask alternative can run locally.
  • History cannot save: download results immediately. Free browser storage before another run.
  • Incident changed: reopen its detail to load the latest state, then reapply your edit.
  • Server is busy: another analysis is running. Retry after it completes. Include the displayed request ID when reporting server errors.

Administrator handover

The source package includes pinned dependencies, Flask APIs, Docker configuration, database backup tooling, tests, methodology, measured results and the client handover checklist. Start with README.md and docs/CLIENT_HANDOVER.md.

This release supports client evaluation and batch investigations. Operational rollout still requires validation on representative client data and agreed accuracy targets. It has no continuous ingestion, multi-machine execution, individual user roles or external notifications. Current sample detection quality is limited; do not use it for unattended incident decisions.
